notes:
Summary: Nimbus is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace an on-prem inference cluster used for a financial customer-facing chat assistant and real-time reranking. Primary goal: strict latency SLOs with deterministic p95 under load and clear measurement alignment between client and server.

Key technical requirements / quotes:
- "We need p95 < 120ms for non-streaming short prompts and streaming-first-byte < 80ms" — CTO (Paraphrase).
- Targets proposed: p50=60ms (non-streaming), p95=120ms, p99=250ms; streaming defined as time-to-first-token + last-token tail of +150ms budget for interactive UX.
- Measurement alignment: Nimbus experienced 30–200ms discrepancies between client-side timers (browser: end-to-end) and server-side (ingress->egress). They want a reproducible spec: server-sent timestamps, sequence numbers for streamed chunks, and canonical definition for "response complete" for streaming flows.
- Important distinctions called out: client-side includes network + TLS handshake + CDN vs server-only request handling. For SLOs they want both: (A) end-to-end p95 for SLA with product team, (B) server-side p95 for capacity planning and credits.
- Warmup / KV-cache notes: cold-model first requests spike p95 by 2–3x — want dedicated pool pre-warm and a guaranteed KV cache policy during POC.
- Throughput/Reserved GPU planning: baseline 400 RPS sustained (chat short prompts) with spiky bursts to 1.8k RPS; Redwood recommended 20–30% headroom on GPU reservation and autoscale burst lanes for peak.
- Streaming vs non-streaming SLOs: define streaming SLOs on last-byte latency for complete responses and time-to-first-byte for perceived latency. Also need per-token throughput SLO for long-form generation jobs.
- Instrumentation ask: provide both server-side histograms (p50/p95/p99) per route/model, and client-side SDK to capture TTFB/TTLB. Correlation IDs must be present in Firehose traces.
- SLA negotiation items: scheduled maintenance windows (prefer Sat 02:00–06:00 local), 99.9% uptime target for dedicated pool, credit formula tied to server-side p95 breaches, and explicit fallbacks to lower-capacity model families.

POC plan (short):
- Week 0: config + model variants onboarded, warmup script
- Week 1: mirrored traffic (10% of prod) to dedicated pool, collect server+client histograms
- Week 2: stress tests for throughput, failover tests, finalize SLA metrics
